output.summary: A herbaceous perennial native to the mountains of southern and central Europe, from the Pyrenees to the Caucasus. Its feathery leaves and softly hairy growth smell strongly of aniseed when crushed. Leaves are sometimes eaten raw or cooked; roots are cooked like parsnips, and seeds are chewed raw.
